title: Let pity answer the unworthy heart
summary: The shabad does not let unworthiness become despair; it places the empty-handed self under divine pity. Gratitude returns when mercy is received without pretending it was earned.
takeaway: Let confessed unworthiness become a doorway to mercy, not self-contempt.
lifeApplication: When shame starts rehearsing what you lack, answer it with the line of mercy: the Lord took pity before you could make yourself worthy.

source.shortMeaning: The line names human lack honestly, then lets the Lord's pity have the stronger word.
source.lifeApplication: When you feel spiritually empty-handed, receive mercy before building a case against yourself.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad turns the admission of no virtue toward the Lord's pity instead of inward collapse.
evidence.turn: Do not make unworthiness the final verdict; let mercy be the voice that answers it.
evidence.practicalImplication: When shame starts rehearsing what you lack, answer it with the line of mercy: the Lord took pity before you could make yourself worthy.
